steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally to make them thinner for quick cooking, then season both sides evenly with salt and black pepper.

recipe.title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Miso Spinach Rice and Green Onion
steps: Finely chop the green onion. Wash the spinach thoroughly, cut it into 4cm lengths, and microwave it in a heat-safe bowl covered with plastic wrap at 600W for 2 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables

recipe.title: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables
steps: Wrap the firm tofu in paper towels to remove excess moisture, then crumble it into small pieces by hand.
Julienne the carrot, and wash the baby spinach and mung bean sprouts thoroughly.

Add the baby spinach to the skillet in the final 1 minute, tossing gently until it wilts completely. Season the vegetable and tofu mixture with soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar, tossing well over medium heat for 1 minute to build a clear, savory profile.
In a separate small pan, fry the 2 eggs over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are slightly crispy, keeping the yolks soft.
Divide the warm cooked rice into two bowls. Arrange the savory tofu and colorful cooked vegetables neatly on top of the rice, and place a fried egg in the center of each bowl.
Taste a small spoonful of the topping before serving; adjust the saltiness with a tiny pinch if needed, and drizzle with the remaining 0.5 tbsp of sesame oil for an extra layer of aroma.
recipe.tips: Sautéeing the tofu until lightly golden removes excess water and concentrates its protein-rich savory flavor, while the splash of vinegar brightens the light seasoning.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice

recipe.title: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice
steps: Chop the broccoli head into small, bite-sized florets and finely dice the tender stalk.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl until well combined.
Heat salad oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until pink and fully cooked through, then push them to the side of the pan.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side of the skillet, stirring gently for 30 seconds until softly scrambled.

Add the broccoli florets and warm white rice to the skillet, breaking up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry everything together over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until the rice grains are lightly toasted and the broccoli is tender-crisp.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a fragrant sear, then season with salt and black pepper. Taste a small bite, adjust with another tiny pinch of salt if needed, and toss well for 1 minute before serving.
recipe.tips: Using warm cooked rice instead of cold refrigerated rice helps it separate easily in a one-pan dish, saving cooking time on a busy weeknight.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry

recipe.title: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry
steps: Core and cut the cabbage into coarse bite-sized pieces (about 4 cm squares) to ensure a crisp texture. Grate the fresh ginger and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the sauce mixture.

Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering. Add the pork slices, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and black pepper, and sear undisturbed for 2 minutes until the bottom turns lightly golden.

Flip the pork and add the cabbage pieces directly into the skillet. Stir-fry briskly over high heat for 3 minutes until the cabbage leaves soften slightly around the edges while retaining a crunchy core.

Pour the ginger-garlic sauce evenly around the edges of the pan so it sizzles and reduces slightly. Toss everything together vigorously for 1 minute until the pork is thoroughly cooked through to the center (exceeding 75 degrees Celsius) and well coated with the glossy sauce. Taste a piece of cabbage; if it needs a sharper edge, adjust with a few drops of soy sauce, then transfer to serving plates immediately.
recipe.tips: To achieve maximum crispness, do not overcrowd the pan and cook over high heat for a short duration. Adding the sauce at the very end prevents the cabbage from releasing too much water and keeps the texture snappy.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice

recipe.title: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice
recipe.dish_badge: One-pan meal with minimal cleanup (2 items)
steps: Slice the beef into bite-sized strips and mix in a bowl with 0.5 tbsp of soy sauce and cooking sake, letting it marinate for 5 minutes. Core and cut the green and red bell peppers into thin strips.
Heat salad oil, minced garlic, and minced ginger in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated beef to the skillet and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until the meat is nearly cooked through and browned on the edges.
Add the bell pepper strips to the skillet and toss continuously over high heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant in color.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a savory aroma, toss everything together for 30 seconds, then taste and adjust saltiness if needed.
Divide the warm cooked white rice into two serving bowls and top generously with the hot beef and bell pepper stir-fry.
recipe.tips: To ensure the beef remains tender without heavy oil, marinate it briefly in sake and soy sauce. High heat cooking for the bell peppers keeps them crisp and locks in their natural sweetness, contrasting nicely with the savory garlic-soy profile.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry

recipe.title: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry
steps: Finely mince the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cut the chicken breast into 2cm bite-sized cubes. Wash the spinach and cut into 4cm lengths.
Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the minced onion and sauté for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and translucent.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, curry powder, and cumin powder to the skillet. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 1 minute until fragrant and aromatic spices bloom.
Add the diced chicken breast to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring until the surface turns white and opaque.

Pour in the canned crushed tomatoes, water, drained chickpeas, salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Remove the lid, add the spinach and butter, and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring gently until the spinach is wilted and tender.

Taste the curry before serving. Adjust the saltiness by adding another pinch of salt if needed, or brighten it with a few drops of vinegar for balance. Ensure the chicken is fully cooked through with an internal temperature reaching 75°C or above.
recipe.tips: Sautéing the onions thoroughly until golden brown provides the deep savory base for this curry. Blooming the spices in oil before adding liquids unlocks their full aromatic potential.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta

recipe.title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta
steps: Finely mince the garlic and cut the chicken breast into bite-sized thin pieces. Clean the mushrooms and separate them into small clusters.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken breast and cook for 4 minutes until the surface turns lightly golden and fully cooked through to the center (ensuring internal temperature reaches 75 degrees Celsius or higher).
Add the minced garlic and mushrooms to the skillet, sautéing over medium heat for 2 minutes until the mushrooms soften and release their savory aroma.
Pour in the milk and water, and bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, add the dry pasta directly into the skillet, breaking it in half if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover with a lid, and simmer for the pasta package cooking time minus 1 minute, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove the lid, stir in the butter, soy sauce, and half of the cheese. Simmer for 1 minute while stirring constantly until the sauce thickens into a rich, creamy consistency.
Taste the sauce before final plating. Adjust the saltiness by adding another 1/8 teaspoon of salt if needed, and enhance the flavor depth with a splash of soy sauce or black pepper.
Transfer to serving plates, top with the remaining cheese and a generous crack of black pepper, and serve immediately.
recipe.tips: Cooking the pasta directly in the milk-water mixture allows the starch from the pasta to naturally thicken the sauce without needing heavy cream. The secret umami boost comes from a small splash of soy sauce, which bridges the gap between the dairy and the savory mushrooms.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Gentle Pumpkin and Soy Milk Soup with Butter-Toasted Bread

recipe.title: Gentle Pumpkin and Soy Milk Soup with Butter-Toasted Bread
steps: Peel the pumpkin and potato, and cut them into 2cm cubes to ensure quick and even cooking.
Heat 10g of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute until melted. Add the pumpkin and potato cubes, and sauté for 3 minutes until coated and lightly softened.
Pour in 100ml of water and 1 tsp of consommé granules. Cover with a lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 6 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender and easily pierced with a fork.
Remove the pan from heat. Use a potato masher or fork to mash about half of the vegetables directly in the pan to create a creamy texture while leaving some chunks for contrast.

Pour in 300ml of unsweetened soy milk and warm gently over low heat for 2 minutes. Do not let it boil vigorously to prevent the soy milk from separating. Stir in 1/4 tsp of salt and a pinch of black pepper, taste, and adjust seasoning if needed.

While the soup is warming, melt the remaining 10g of butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Toast the thick-sliced bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Ladle the warm pumpkin and soy milk soup into bowls and serve immediately alongside the hot buttered toast.
recipe.tips: To prevent the soy milk from curdling, always add it after simmering the vegetables and keep the heat low without letting it boil. The combination of sweet pumpkin and savory soy milk creates a rich profile with reduced sodium.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt

recipe.title: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt
steps: Slice the tomatoes into bite-sized wedges and toss them in a small bowl with half of the lemon juice (1.5 tsp), a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper to create a refreshing side salad.
In a separate small bowl, mash the ripe avocado with the remaining lemon juice, minced garlic, 1/8 tsp of salt, and a pinch of black pepper until mostly smooth yet slightly chunky.
Melt the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Crack the eggs into the pan and fry for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and opaque, but the yolks remain soft and runny.
Toast the thick-cut bread slices in a toaster or the same skillet for 2 minutes on medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy on the edges.

Spread the seasoned mashed avocado evenly across the warm toasted bread slices. Gently place one fried egg on top of each toast. Taste a small bite of the avocado and egg, then adjust with an extra tiny pinch of salt or pepper if needed before serving alongside the tomato salad and plain yogurt.
recipe.tips: To elevate the flavor profile without adding excess salt, ensure the lemon juice and garlic are thoroughly mixed into the avocado to provide a vibrant acidic contrast to the rich egg yolk.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce

recipe.title: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the baby potatoes in half and boil them in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp of water covered for 4 minutes until slightly tender. Snap off the tough ends of the asparagus and cut them in half.
Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels and season both sides evenly with half of the salt (1/4 tsp) and a pinch of black pepper.

In a large oven-safe skillet, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Place the cod fillets in the center and arrange the parboiled potatoes and asparagus around them. Sear the cod for 2 minutes until the bottom edges turn lightly golden.
In a small bowl, mix the melted butter, minced garlic, lemon juice, and the remaining 1/4 tsp of salt. Pour this zesty lemon-butter mixture evenly over the fish and vegetables in the skillet.

Transfer the skillet directly into the preheated oven and bake at 200°C for 12 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and its internal temperature reaches 63°C or higher. Taste the sauce in the pan before serving; if needed, adjust with a tiny pinch of salt or a drop of lemon juice to ensure a bright, well-defined flavor profile.
Plate the baked cod alongside the roasted potatoes and tender-crisp asparagus, spooning the pan juices over the top to finish.
recipe.tips: For maximum flavor contrast, make sure to pat the cod completely dry before searing so it develops a light crust, while the lemon juice cuts through the richness of the butter.

Heat 10g of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute until melted. Add the pumpkin and potato cubes, and sauté for 3 minutes until coated and lightly softened.
Pour in 100ml of water and 1 tsp of consommé granules. Cover with a lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 6 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender and easily pierced with a fork.
Remove the pan from heat. Use a potato masher or fork to mash about half of the vegetables directly in the pan to create a creamy texture while leaving some chunks for contrast.

Pour in 300ml of unsweetened soy milk and warm gently over low heat for 2 minutes. Do not let it boil vigorously to prevent the soy milk from separating. Stir in 1/4 tsp of salt and a pinch of black pepper, taste, and adjust seasoning if needed.

While the soup is warming, melt the remaining 10g of butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Toast the thick-sliced bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Ladle the warm pumpkin and soy milk soup into bowls and serve immediately alongside the hot buttered toast.
recipe.tips: To prevent the soy milk from curdling, always add it after simmering the vegetables and keep the heat low without letting it boil. The combination of sweet pumpkin and savory soy milk creates a rich profile with reduced sodium.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt

recipe.title: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt
steps: Slice the tomatoes into bite-sized wedges and toss them in a small bowl with half of the lemon juice (1.5 tsp), a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper to create a refreshing side salad.
In a separate small bowl, mash the ripe avocado with the remaining lemon juice, minced garlic, 1/8 tsp of salt, and a pinch of black pepper until mostly smooth yet slightly chunky.
Melt the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Crack the eggs into the pan and fry for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and opaque, but the yolks remain soft and runny.
Toast the thick-cut bread slices in a toaster or the same skillet for 2 minutes on medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy on the edges.

Spread the seasoned mashed avocado evenly across the warm toasted bread slices. Gently place one fried egg on top of each toast. Taste a small bite of the avocado and egg, then adjust with an extra tiny pinch of salt or pepper if needed before serving alongside the tomato salad and plain yogurt.
recipe.tips: To elevate the flavor profile without adding excess salt, ensure the lemon juice and garlic are thoroughly mixed into the avocado to provide a vibrant acidic contrast to the rich egg yolk.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce

recipe.title: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the baby potatoes in half and boil them in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp of water covered for 4 minutes until slightly tender. Snap off the tough ends of the asparagus and cut them in half.
Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels and season both sides evenly with half of the salt (1/4 tsp) and a pinch of black pepper.

In a large oven-safe skillet, heat the olive oil over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Place the cod fillets in the center and arrange the parboiled potatoes and asparagus around them. Sear the cod for 2 minutes until the bottom edges turn lightly golden.
In a small bowl, mix the melted butter, minced garlic, lemon juice, and the remaining 1/4 tsp of salt. Pour this zesty lemon-butter mixture evenly over the fish and vegetables in the skillet.

Transfer the skillet directly into the preheated oven and bake at 200°C for 12 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and its internal temperature reaches 63°C or higher. Taste the sauce in the pan before serving; if needed, adjust with a tiny pinch of salt or a drop of lemon juice to ensure a bright, well-defined flavor profile.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Warming Lentil, Sweet Potato, and Kale Soup with Crispy Garlic Chickpea Topping

recipe.title: Warming Lentil, Sweet Potato, and Kale Soup with Crispy Garlic Chickpea Topping

Taste the soup. Adjust the saltiness by adding a pinch of salt (about 1/8 tsp at a time) if needed, and stir in the lemon juice for a bright, balancing acidity. Divide into bowls and top with the crispy garlic chickpeas and freshly cracked black pepper.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Carrots

recipe.title: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Carrots
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally to make them thinner for quick cooking, then season both sides evenly with salt and black pepper.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets, slice the carrot into 5mm thick rounds, and finely mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Place the chicken fillets in the pan and sear for 3 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown.

Flip the chicken, then arrange the broccoli florets and carrot slices around the chicken in the same pan. Add the water, cover with a lid, and steam-cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C or higher.

Remove the lid, turn the heat to medium-high, add the minced garlic, butter, and lemon juice to the pan. Toss the vegetables and spoon the melted butter-lemon sauce over the chicken for 1 minute until fragrant and slightly reduced.
Taste the sauce carefully and add a tiny pinch of salt or a splash of lemon juice if needed to balance the flavor. Turn off the heat and serve immediately.
recipe.tips: Slicing the chicken breasts thinly ensures they cook evenly and stay juicy in just one pan without drying out. The bright lemon juice and aromatic garlic elevate the light seasoning, keeping the dish protein-packed yet refreshing.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Pan-Seared Salmon with Miso Spinach Rice and Green Onion

recipe.title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Miso Spinach Rice and Green Onion
steps: Finely chop the green onion. Wash the spinach thoroughly, cut it into 4cm lengths, and microwave it in a heat-safe bowl covered with plastic wrap at 600W for 2 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
In a small bowl, combine the miso paste, mirin, and water to create a savory glaze.
Season the salmon fillets evenly with a pinch of salt and black pepper.

Heat salad oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Place the salmon skin-side down and sear for 4 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy. Flip and cook for another 3 minutes until fully cooked through.

Reduce the heat to low. Add the cooked rice, squeezed spinach, chopped green onion, and the miso glaze directly into the pan around the salmon. Toss the ingredients together for 2 minutes until the rice is heated through and well coated with the savory miso flavor.
Taste a small spoonful of the miso rice before serving to check the balance. Divide the vibrant green onion spinach rice and the seared salmon onto two plates and serve immediately while hot.
recipe.tips: Balancing the savory miso with the natural sweetness of mirin creates a rich flavor profile without needing excess salt. Sear the salmon skin-side down first to achieve a crispy texture that contrasts with the tender rice.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables

recipe.title: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables
steps: Wrap the firm tofu in paper towels to remove excess moisture, then crumble it into small pieces by hand.
Julienne the carrot, and wash the baby spinach and mung bean sprouts thoroughly.

Heat half of the sesame oil (0.5 tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and crumbled tofu. Stir-fry for 4 minutes until the tofu is lightly browned and aromatic.
Push the tofu to one side of the pan. Add the carrot julienne and mung bean sprouts to the other side, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and sauté over medium heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.

Add the baby spinach to the skillet in the final 1 minute, tossing gently until it wilts completely. Season the vegetable and tofu mixture with soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar, tossing well over medium heat for 1 minute to build a clear, savory profile.
In a separate small pan, fry the 2 eggs over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are slightly crispy, keeping the yolks soft.
Divide the warm cooked rice into two bowls. Arrange the savory tofu and colorful cooked vegetables neatly on top of the rice, and place a fried egg in the center of each bowl.
Taste a small spoonful of the topping before serving; adjust the saltiness with a tiny pinch if needed, and drizzle with the remaining 0.5 tbsp of sesame oil for an extra layer of aroma.
recipe.tips: Sautéeing the tofu until lightly golden removes excess water and concentrates its protein-rich savory flavor, while the splash of vinegar brightens the light seasoning.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice

recipe.title: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice
steps: Chop the broccoli head into small, bite-sized florets and finely dice the tender stalk.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl until well combined.
Heat salad oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until pink and fully cooked through, then push them to the side of the pan.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side of the skillet, stirring gently for 30 seconds until softly scrambled.

Add the broccoli florets and warm white rice to the skillet, breaking up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry everything together over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until the rice grains are lightly toasted and the broccoli is tender-crisp.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a fragrant sear, then season with salt and black pepper. Taste a small bite, adjust with another tiny pinch of salt if needed, and toss well for 1 minute before serving.
recipe.tips: Using warm cooked rice instead of cold refrigerated rice helps it separate easily in a one-pan dish, saving cooking time on a busy weeknight.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry

recipe.title: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry
steps: Core and cut the cabbage into coarse bite-sized pieces (about 4 cm squares) to ensure a crisp texture. Grate the fresh ginger and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the sauce mixture.

Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering. Add the pork slices, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and black pepper, and sear undisturbed for 2 minutes until the bottom turns lightly golden.

Flip the pork and add the cabbage pieces directly into the skillet. Stir-fry briskly over high heat for 3 minutes until the cabbage leaves soften slightly around the edges while retaining a crunchy core.

Pour the ginger-garlic sauce evenly around the edges of the pan so it sizzles and reduces slightly. Toss everything together vigorously for 1 minute until the pork is thoroughly cooked through to the center (exceeding 75 degrees Celsius) and well coated with the glossy sauce. Taste a piece of cabbage; if it needs a sharper edge, adjust with a few drops of soy sauce, then transfer to serving plates immediately.
recipe.tips: To achieve maximum crispness, do not overcrowd the pan and cook over high heat for a short duration. Adding the sauce at the very end prevents the cabbage from releasing too much water and keeps the texture snappy.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice

recipe.title: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice
recipe.dish_badge: One-pan meal with minimal cleanup (2 items)
steps: Slice the beef into bite-sized strips and mix in a bowl with 0.5 tbsp of soy sauce and cooking sake, letting it marinate for 5 minutes. Core and cut the green and red bell peppers into thin strips.
Heat salad oil, minced garlic, and minced ginger in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated beef to the skillet and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until the meat is nearly cooked through and browned on the edges.
Add the bell pepper strips to the skillet and toss continuously over high heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant in color.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a savory aroma, toss everything together for 30 seconds, then taste and adjust saltiness if needed.
Divide the warm cooked white rice into two serving bowls and top generously with the hot beef and bell pepper stir-fry.
recipe.tips: To ensure the beef remains tender without heavy oil, marinate it briefly in sake and soy sauce. High heat cooking for the bell peppers keeps them crisp and locks in their natural sweetness, contrasting nicely with the savory garlic-soy profile.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry

recipe.title: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry
steps: Finely mince the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cut the chicken breast into 2cm bite-sized cubes. Wash the spinach and cut into 4cm lengths.
Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the minced onion and sauté for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and translucent.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, curry powder, and cumin powder to the skillet. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 1 minute until fragrant and aromatic spices bloom.
Add the diced chicken breast to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring until the surface turns white and opaque.

Pour in the canned crushed tomatoes, water, drained chickpeas, salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Remove the lid, add the spinach and butter, and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring gently until the spinach is wilted and tender.

Taste the curry before serving. Adjust the saltiness by adding another pinch of salt if needed, or brighten it with a few drops of vinegar for balance. Ensure the chicken is fully cooked through with an internal temperature reaching 75°C or above.
recipe.tips: Sautéing the onions thoroughly until golden brown provides the deep savory base for this curry. Blooming the spices in oil before adding liquids unlocks their full aromatic potential.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta

recipe.title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta
steps: Finely mince the garlic and cut the chicken breast into bite-sized thin pieces. Clean the mushrooms and separate them into small clusters.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken breast and cook for 4 minutes until the surface turns lightly golden and fully cooked through to the center (ensuring internal temperature reaches 75 degrees Celsius or higher).
Add the minced garlic and mushrooms to the skillet, sautéing over medium heat for 2 minutes until the mushrooms soften and release their savory aroma.
Pour in the milk and water, and bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, add the dry pasta directly into the skillet, breaking it in half if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover with a lid, and simmer for the pasta package cooking time minus 1 minute, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove the lid, stir in the butter, soy sauce, and half of the cheese. Simmer for 1 minute while stirring constantly until the sauce thickens into a rich, creamy consistency.
Taste the sauce before final plating. Adjust the saltiness by adding another 1/8 teaspoon of salt if needed, and enhance the flavor depth with a splash of soy sauce or black pepper.
Transfer to serving plates, top with the remaining cheese and a generous crack of black pepper, and serve immediately.
recipe.tips: Cooking the pasta directly in the milk-water mixture allows the starch from the pasta to naturally thicken the sauce without needing heavy cream. The secret umami boost comes from a small splash of soy sauce, which bridges the gap between the dairy and the savory mushrooms.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice

recipe.title: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice
recipe.dish_badge: One-pan meal with minimal cleanup (2 items)
steps: Slice the beef into bite-sized strips and mix in a bowl with 0.5 tbsp of soy sauce and cooking sake, letting it marinate for 5 minutes. Core and cut the green and red bell peppers into thin strips.
Heat salad oil, minced garlic, and minced ginger in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated beef to the skillet and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until the meat is nearly cooked through and browned on the edges.
Add the bell pepper strips to the skillet and toss continuously over high heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant in color.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a savory aroma, toss everything together for 30 seconds, then taste and adjust saltiness if needed.
Divide the warm cooked white rice into two serving bowls and top generously with the hot beef and bell pepper stir-fry.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry

recipe.title: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry
steps: Finely mince the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cut the chicken breast into 2cm bite-sized cubes. Wash the spinach and cut into 4cm lengths.
Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the minced onion and sauté for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and translucent.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, curry powder, and cumin powder to the skillet. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 1 minute until fragrant and aromatic spices bloom.
Add the diced chicken breast to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring until the surface turns white and opaque.

Pour in the canned crushed tomatoes, water, drained chickpeas, salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Remove the lid, add the spinach and butter, and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring gently until the spinach is wilted and tender.

Taste the curry before serving. Adjust the saltiness by adding another pinch of salt if needed, or brighten it with a few drops of vinegar for balance. Ensure the chicken is fully cooked through with an internal temperature reaching 75°C or above.
recipe.tips: Sautéing the onions thoroughly until golden brown provides the deep savory base for this curry. Blooming the spices in oil before adding liquids unlocks their full aromatic potential.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta

recipe.title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta
steps: Finely mince the garlic and cut the chicken breast into bite-sized thin pieces. Clean the mushrooms and separate them into small clusters.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken breast and cook for 4 minutes until the surface turns lightly golden and fully cooked through to the center (ensuring internal temperature reaches 75 degrees Celsius or higher).
Add the minced garlic and mushrooms to the skillet, sautéing over medium heat for 2 minutes until the mushrooms soften and release their savory aroma.
Pour in the milk and water, and bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, add the dry pasta directly into the skillet, breaking it in half if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover with a lid, and simmer for the pasta package cooking time minus 1 minute, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove the lid, stir in the butter, soy sauce, and half of the cheese. Simmer for 1 minute while stirring constantly until the sauce thickens into a rich, creamy consistency.

Transfer to serving plates, top with the remaining cheese and a generous crack of black pepper, and serve immediately.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Gentle Pumpkin and Soy Milk Soup with Butter-Toasted Bread

recipe.title: Gentle Pumpkin and Soy Milk Soup with Butter-Toasted Bread
steps: Peel the pumpkin and potato, and cut them into 2cm cubes to ensure quick and even cooking.
Heat 10g of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute until melted. Add the pumpkin and potato cubes, and sauté for 3 minutes until coated and lightly softened.
Pour in 100ml of water and 1 tsp of consommé granules. Cover with a lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 6 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender and easily pierced with a fork.
Remove the pan from heat. Use a potato masher or fork to mash about half of the vegetables directly in the pan to create a creamy texture while leaving some chunks for contrast.

Pour in 300ml of unsweetened soy milk and warm gently over low heat for 2 minutes. Do not let it boil vigorously to prevent the soy milk from separating. Stir in 1/4 tsp of salt and a pinch of black pepper, taste, and adjust seasoning if needed.

While the soup is warming, melt the remaining 10g of butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Toast the thick-sliced bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Ladle the warm pumpkin and soy milk soup into bowls and serve immediately alongside the hot buttered toast.
recipe.tips: To prevent the soy milk from curdling, always add it after simmering the vegetables and keep the heat low without letting it boil. The combination of sweet pumpkin and savory soy milk creates a rich profile with reduced sodium.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt

recipe.title: High-Protein Avocado and Egg Breakfast Toast with Fresh Tomato Salad and Yogurt
steps: Slice the tomatoes into bite-sized wedges and toss them in a small bowl with half of the lemon juice (1.5 tsp), a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper to create a refreshing side salad.
In a separate small bowl, mash the ripe avocado with the remaining lemon juice, minced garlic, 1/8 tsp of salt, and a pinch of black pepper until mostly smooth yet slightly chunky.
Melt the butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Crack the eggs into the pan and fry for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and opaque, but the yolks remain soft and runny.
Toast the thick-cut bread slices in a toaster or the same skillet for 2 minutes on medium-high heat until golden brown and crispy on the edges.

Spread the seasoned mashed avocado evenly across the warm toasted bread slices. Gently place one fried egg on top of each toast. Taste a small bite of the avocado and egg, then adjust with an extra tiny pinch of salt or pepper if needed before serving alongside the tomato salad and plain yogurt.
recipe.tips: To elevate the flavor profile without adding excess salt, ensure the lemon juice and garlic are thoroughly mixed into the avocado to provide a vibrant acidic contrast to the rich egg yolk.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce

recipe.title: One-Pan Baked Cod with Asparagus, Potatoes, and Zesty Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the baby potatoes in half and boil them in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp of water covered for 4 minutes until slightly tender. Snap off the tough ends of the asparagus and cut them in half.
Pat the cod fillets dry with paper towels and season both sides evenly with half of the salt (1/4 tsp) and a pinch of black pepper.

In a small bowl, mix the melted butter, minced garlic, lemon juice, and the remaining 1/4 tsp of salt. Pour this zesty lemon-butter mixture evenly over the fish and vegetables in the skillet.

Transfer the skillet directly into the preheated oven and bake at 200°C for 12 minutes, or until the cod flakes easily with a fork and its internal temperature reaches 63°C or higher. Taste the sauce in the pan before serving; if needed, adjust with a tiny pinch of salt or a drop of lemon juice to ensure a bright, well-defined flavor profile.
Plate the baked cod alongside the roasted potatoes and tender-crisp asparagus, spooning the pan juices over the top to finish.
recipe.tips: For maximum flavor contrast, make sure to pat the cod completely dry before searing so it develops a light crust, while the lemon juice cuts through the richness of the butter.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Warming Lentil, Sweet Potato, and Kale Soup with Crispy Garlic Chickpea Topping

recipe.title: Warming Lentil, Sweet Potato, and Kale Soup with Crispy Garlic Chickpea Topping

recipe.tips: For the perfect high-protein light seasoning balance, we rely on the natural sweetness of sweet potatoes, the earthy depth of lentils, and a splash of lemon juice at the end to elevate the flavors without adding excess sodium. cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Carrots

recipe.title: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Carrots
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally to make them thinner for quick cooking, then season both sides evenly with salt and black pepper.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets, slice the carrot into 5mm thick rounds, and finely mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Place the chicken fillets in the pan and sear for 3 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown.

Flip the chicken, then arrange the broccoli florets and carrot slices around the chicken in the same pan. Add the water, cover with a lid, and steam-cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C or higher.

Remove the lid, turn the heat to medium-high, add the minced garlic, butter, and lemon juice to the pan. Toss the vegetables and spoon the melted butter-lemon sauce over the chicken for 1 minute until fragrant and slightly reduced.
Taste the sauce carefully and add a tiny pinch of salt or a splash of lemon juice if needed to balance the flavor. Turn off the heat and serve immediately.
recipe.tips: Slicing the chicken breasts thinly ensures they cook evenly and stay juicy in just one pan without drying out. The bright lemon juice and aromatic garlic elevate the light seasoning, keeping the dish protein-packed yet refreshing.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Pan-Seared Salmon with Miso Spinach Rice and Green Onion

recipe.title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Miso Spinach Rice and Green Onion
steps: Finely chop the green onion. Wash the spinach thoroughly, cut it into 4cm lengths, and microwave it in a heat-safe bowl covered with plastic wrap at 600W for 2 minutes, then squeeze out excess water.
In a small bowl, combine the miso paste, mirin, and water to create a savory glaze.
Season the salmon fillets evenly with a pinch of salt and black pepper.

Heat salad oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Place the salmon skin-side down and sear for 4 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy. Flip and cook for another 3 minutes until fully cooked through.

Reduce the heat to low. Add the cooked rice, squeezed spinach, chopped green onion, and the miso glaze directly into the pan around the salmon. Toss the ingredients together for 2 minutes until the rice is heated through and well coated with the savory miso flavor.
Taste a small spoonful of the miso rice before serving to check the balance. Divide the vibrant green onion spinach rice and the seared salmon onto two plates and serve immediately while hot.
recipe.tips: Balancing the savory miso with the natural sweetness of mirin creates a rich flavor profile without needing excess salt. Sear the salmon skin-side down first to achieve a crispy texture that contrasts with the tender rice.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables

recipe.title: Colorful Tofu and Egg Bibimbap with Vegetables
steps: Wrap the firm tofu in paper towels to remove excess moisture, then crumble it into small pieces by hand.
Julienne the carrot, and wash the baby spinach and mung bean sprouts thoroughly.

Heat half of the sesame oil (0.5 tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and crumbled tofu. Stir-fry for 4 minutes until the tofu is lightly browned and aromatic.
Push the tofu to one side of the pan. Add the carrot julienne and mung bean sprouts to the other side, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and sauté over medium heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.

Add the baby spinach to the skillet in the final 1 minute, tossing gently until it wilts completely. Season the vegetable and tofu mixture with soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar, tossing well over medium heat for 1 minute to build a clear, savory profile.
In a separate small pan, fry the 2 eggs over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are slightly crispy, keeping the yolks soft.
Divide the warm cooked rice into two bowls. Arrange the savory tofu and colorful cooked vegetables neatly on top of the rice, and place a fried egg in the center of each bowl.
Taste a small spoonful of the topping before serving; adjust the saltiness with a tiny pinch if needed, and drizzle with the remaining 0.5 tbsp of sesame oil for an extra layer of aroma.
recipe.tips: Sautéeing the tofu until lightly golden removes excess water and concentrates its protein-rich savory flavor, while the splash of vinegar brightens the light seasoning.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice

recipe.title: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice
steps: Chop the broccoli head into small, bite-sized florets and finely dice the tender stalk.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl until well combined.
Heat salad oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until pink and fully cooked through, then push them to the side of the pan.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side of the skillet, stirring gently for 30 seconds until softly scrambled.

Add the broccoli florets and warm white rice to the skillet, breaking up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry everything together over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until the rice grains are lightly toasted and the broccoli is tender-crisp.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a fragrant sear, then season with salt and black pepper. Taste a small bite, adjust with another tiny pinch of salt if needed, and toss well for 1 minute before serving.
recipe.tips: Using warm cooked rice instead of cold refrigerated rice helps it separate easily in a one-pan dish, saving cooking time on a busy weeknight.

feedback.comment: Delicious, practical, and worth making again.

cooked_records.recipeTitle: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry

recipe.title: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry
steps: Core and cut the cabbage into coarse bite-sized pieces (about 4 cm squares) to ensure a crisp texture. Grate the fresh ginger and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the sauce mixture.

Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering. Add the pork slices, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and black pepper, and sear undisturbed for 2 minutes until the bottom turns lightly golden.

Flip the pork and add the cabbage pieces directly into the skillet. Stir-fry briskly over high heat for 3 minutes until the cabbage leaves soften slightly around the edges while retaining a crunchy core.

Pour the ginger-garlic sauce evenly around the edges of the pan so it sizzles and reduces slightly. Toss everything together vigorously for 1 minute until the pork is thoroughly cooked through to the center (exceeding 75 degrees Celsius) and well coated with the glossy sauce. Taste a piece of cabbage; if it needs a sharper edge, adjust with a few drops of soy sauce, then transfer to serving plates immediately.
recipe.tips: To achieve maximum crispness, do not overcrowd the pan and cook over high heat for a short duration. Adding the sauce at the very end prevents the cabbage from releasing too much water and keeps the texture snappy.

Julienne the carrot, and wash the baby spinach and mung bean sprouts thoroughly.

Heat half of the sesame oil (0.5 tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the minced garlic, ginger, and crumbled tofu. Stir-fry for 4 minutes until the tofu is lightly browned and aromatic.
Push the tofu to one side of the pan. Add the carrot julienne and mung bean sprouts to the other side, sprinkle with a pinch of salt, and sauté over medium heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.

Add the baby spinach to the skillet in the final 1 minute, tossing gently until it wilts completely. Season the vegetable and tofu mixture with soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar, tossing well over medium heat for 1 minute to build a clear, savory profile.
In a separate small pan, fry the 2 eggs over medium heat for 3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are slightly crispy, keeping the yolks soft.
Divide the warm cooked rice into two bowls. Arrange the savory tofu and colorful cooked vegetables neatly on top of the rice, and place a fried egg in the center of each bowl.
Taste a small spoonful of the topping before serving; adjust the saltiness with a tiny pinch if needed, and drizzle with the remaining 0.5 tbsp of sesame oil for an extra layer of aroma.
recipe.tips: Sautéeing the tofu until lightly golden removes excess water and concentrates its protein-rich savory flavor, while the splash of vinegar brightens the light seasoning.

recipe.title: One-Pan High-Protein Shrimp and Broccoli Fried Rice
steps: Chop the broccoli head into small, bite-sized florets and finely dice the tender stalk.
Beat the eggs in a small bowl until well combined.
Heat salad oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and grated ginger, sautéing for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes until pink and fully cooked through, then push them to the side of the pan.
Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side of the skillet, stirring gently for 30 seconds until softly scrambled.

Add the broccoli florets and warm white rice to the skillet, breaking up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry everything together over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until the rice grains are lightly toasted and the broccoli is tender-crisp.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a fragrant sear, then season with salt and black pepper. Taste a small bite, adjust with another tiny pinch of salt if needed, and toss well for 1 minute before serving.
recipe.tips: Using warm cooked rice instead of cold refrigerated rice helps it separate easily in a one-pan dish, saving cooking time on a busy weeknight.

recipe.title: Crispy Ginger Pork and Cabbage Stir-Fry
steps: Core and cut the cabbage into coarse bite-sized pieces (about 4 cm squares) to ensure a crisp texture. Grate the fresh ginger and mince the garlic.
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the sauce mixture.

Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering. Add the pork slices, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and black pepper, and sear undisturbed for 2 minutes until the bottom turns lightly golden.

Flip the pork and add the cabbage pieces directly into the skillet. Stir-fry briskly over high heat for 3 minutes until the cabbage leaves soften slightly around the edges while retaining a crunchy core.

Pour the ginger-garlic sauce evenly around the edges of the pan so it sizzles and reduces slightly. Toss everything together vigorously for 1 minute until the pork is thoroughly cooked through to the center (exceeding 75 degrees Celsius) and well coated with the glossy sauce. Taste a piece of cabbage; if it needs a sharper edge, adjust with a few drops of soy sauce, then transfer to serving plates immediately.
recipe.tips: To achieve maximum crispness, do not overcrowd the pan and cook over high heat for a short duration. Adding the sauce at the very end prevents the cabbage from releasing too much water and keeps the texture snappy.

recipe.title: High-Protein Tender Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry with Steamed Rice
recipe.dish_badge: One-pan meal with minimal cleanup (2 items)
steps: Slice the beef into bite-sized strips and mix in a bowl with 0.5 tbsp of soy sauce and cooking sake, letting it marinate for 5 minutes. Core and cut the green and red bell peppers into thin strips.
Heat salad oil, minced garlic, and minced ginger in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated beef to the skillet and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes until the meat is nearly cooked through and browned on the edges.
Add the bell pepper strips to the skillet and toss continuously over high heat for 3 minutes until tender-crisp and vibrant in color.

Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp of soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil around the edges of the pan to create a savory aroma, toss everything together for 30 seconds, then taste and adjust saltiness if needed.
Divide the warm cooked white rice into two serving bowls and top generously with the hot beef and bell pepper stir-fry.
recipe.tips: To ensure the beef remains tender without heavy oil, marinate it briefly in sake and soy sauce. High heat cooking for the bell peppers keeps them crisp and locks in their natural sweetness, contrasting nicely with the savory garlic-soy profile.

recipe.title: High-Protein Tomato Chickpea and Spinach Curry
steps: Finely mince the onion, garlic, and ginger. Cut the chicken breast into 2cm bite-sized cubes. Wash the spinach and cut into 4cm lengths.
Heat the salad oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the minced onion and sauté for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and translucent.
Add the minced garlic, ginger, curry powder, and cumin powder to the skillet. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 1 minute until fragrant and aromatic spices bloom.
Add the diced chicken breast to the skillet and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring until the surface turns white and opaque.

Pour in the canned crushed tomatoes, water, drained chickpeas, salt, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Remove the lid, add the spinach and butter, and cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring gently until the spinach is wilted and tender.

Taste the curry before serving. Adjust the saltiness by adding another pinch of salt if needed, or brighten it with a few drops of vinegar for balance. Ensure the chicken is fully cooked through with an internal temperature reaching 75°C or above.
recipe.tips: Sautéing the onions thoroughly until golden brown provides the deep savory base for this curry. Blooming the spices in oil before adding liquids unlocks their full aromatic potential.

recipe.title: Creamy Garlic Mushroom and Chicken Pasta
steps: Finely mince the garlic and cut the chicken breast into bite-sized thin pieces. Clean the mushrooms and separate them into small clusters.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken breast and cook for 4 minutes until the surface turns lightly golden and fully cooked through to the center (ensuring internal temperature reaches 75 degrees Celsius or higher).
Add the minced garlic and mushrooms to the skillet, sautéing over medium heat for 2 minutes until the mushrooms soften and release their savory aroma.
Pour in the milk and water, and bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, add the dry pasta directly into the skillet, breaking it in half if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover with a lid, and simmer for the pasta package cooking time minus 1 minute, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove the lid, stir in the butter, soy sauce, and half of the cheese. Simmer for 1 minute while stirring constantly until the sauce thickens into a rich, creamy consistency.
Taste the sauce before final plating. Adjust the saltiness by adding another 1/8 teaspoon of salt if needed, and enhance the flavor depth with a splash of soy sauce or black pepper.
Transfer to serving plates, top with the remaining cheese and a generous crack of black pepper, and serve immediately.
recipe.tips: Cooking the pasta directly in the milk-water mixture allows the starch from the pasta to naturally thicken the sauce without needing heavy cream. The secret umami boost comes from a small splash of soy sauce, which bridges the gap between the dairy and the savory mushrooms.

recipe.title: Gentle Pumpkin and Soy Milk Soup with Butter-Toasted Bread
steps: Peel the pumpkin and potato, and cut them into 2cm cubes to ensure quick and even cooking.
Heat 10g of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 1 minute until melted. Add the pumpkin and potato cubes, and sauté for 3 minutes until coated and lightly softened.
Pour in 100ml of water and 1 tsp of consommé granules. Cover with a lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 6 minutes until the vegetables are completely tender and easily pierced with a fork.
Remove the pan from heat. Use a potato masher or fork to mash about half of the vegetables directly in the pan to create a creamy texture while leaving some chunks for contrast.

Pour in 300ml of unsweetened soy milk and warm gently over low heat for 2 minutes. Do not let it boil vigorously to prevent the soy milk from separating. Stir in 1/4 tsp of salt and a pinch of black pepper, taste, and adjust seasoning if needed.

While the soup is warming, melt the remaining 10g of butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Toast the thick-sliced bread for 2 minutes on each side until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
Ladle the warm pumpkin and soy milk soup into bowls and serve immediately alongside the hot buttered toast.
recipe.tips: To prevent the soy milk from curdling, always add it after simmering the vegetables and keep the heat low without letting it boil. The combination of sweet pumpkin and savory soy milk creates a rich profile with reduced sodium.

recipes.title: One-Pan Lemon Garlic Chicken with Broccoli and Carrots
steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally to make them thinner for quick cooking, then season both sides evenly with salt and black pepper.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets, slice the carrot into 5mm thick rounds, and finely mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Place the chicken fillets in the pan and sear for 3 minutes until the bottom turns golden brown.

Flip the chicken, then arrange the broccoli florets and carrot slices around the chicken in the same pan. Add the water, cover with a lid, and steam-cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp and the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C or higher.

Remove the lid, turn the heat to medium-high, add the minced garlic, butter, and lemon juice to the pan. Toss the vegetables and spoon the melted butter-lemon sauce over the chicken for 1 minute until fragrant and slightly reduced.
Taste the sauce carefully and add a tiny pinch of salt or a splash of lemon juice if needed to balance the flavor. Turn off the heat and serve immediately.
recipes.tips: Slicing the chicken breasts thinly ensures they cook evenly and stay juicy in just one pan without drying out. The bright lemon juice and aromatic garlic elevate the light seasoning, keeping the dish protein-packed yet refreshing.

cookingTips.tip: Store raw chicken in the coldest part of the refrigerator or freeze it if not using within two days. Keep broccoli in a perforated bag in the crisper drawer to maintain freshness.
Adding the lemon juice and butter at the very end prevents the butter from separating and keeps the bright citrus aroma vibrant and punchy.
Chicken breast is an excellent source of lean high-quality protein, while broccoli and carrots provide abundant vitamin C and beta-carotene to support recovery and immune health.
